title: The Rust Vein Where Metal Learns Singing

features.name: the singing rust-vein
features.desc-on-touch: Iron oxide arranged in a vertical seam. It hums. The rust is singing the metal's slow transformation into something else, something lighter.

features.name: the threshold becoming kind
features.desc-on-touch: An arch where the metal is learning to hold both sides without keeping them separate. Rust has taught it how to be permeable without losing its form.

features.name: the oxidation-bloom
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of dissolved iron, rich and orange-red. The metal is blooming as it oxidizes. Each rust-flower is a note in a centuries-long melody.

features.name: the metal's memory-song
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe shape holding the metal's original song—the resonance it held before rust taught it new harmonies. Both songs play at once now.

features.name: the permeability-edge
features.desc-on-touch: Where the metal has become transparent enough to see through. Rust has dissolved the boundary between inside and outside. Both are one threshold now.

features.name: the dissolution-music
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of pure song—the sound that metal makes as it transforms through rust into earth, into oxygen, into air. The sound of something learning to let go.

inscription: rust is the sound metal makes when it learns to sing its own becoming
